biggest_catch: The $25 activation bonus is real and fixed, but the rest of the value proposition depends on the plan's supply rate versus your utility — a competitive rate today can become a worse-than-utility rate later, so compare the actual cents-per-kWh before enrolling; the 5% cash back applies only to the supply portion of the bill, not delivery charges.
catches: You must enroll electricity supply through a participating heating oil dealer referral link to get the referral-program terms.
The $25 activation bonus is paid per meter you sign up.
The 5% annual cash back applies only to the supply portion of the electricity bill, not the full bill or delivery charges.

The page says customers are 'currently saving with competitive rates versus your local utility' — plan rates can change; compare the actual supply rate to your utility's default rate before enrolling.
Early signup does not require a long-term commitment per the page ('no risk, fees, or long-term commitment'), but confirm plan terms at enrollment.
The rewards offset planned electricity spending (savings), never income.
Only available in states where Energy Plus supplies residential electricity.

The official page does not specify whether the $25 activation bonus is paid as a bill credit or by check; only the fixed $25/meter amount is counted (the 5% annual supply-charge cash back is variable and excluded from the payout figure).
